# E0506: `catch` around a failure that belongs to the caller

The failures of a function parameter belong to your caller, unless its type names their error. Write `raise<E>` in the parameter's row to handle them here.

- Rule: [`effects.catch-around-row-variables`](../../reference/12-effects.md#effects.catch-around-row-variables)
- Reported at: the call.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `analyses` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0506:8
type ParseError = | Empty

fn parse(text: str) -> i64 / raise<ParseError> { raise Empty }

fn safe(text: str, fallback: fn() -> i64) -> i64 {
  try {
    let n = parse(text)
    n + fallback()
  }
    catch _ because "a failure counts as zero" => 0
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
type ParseError = | Empty

fn parse(text: str) -> i64 / raise<ParseError> { raise Empty }

fn safe(text: str, fallback: fn() -> i64) -> i64 {
  let n = try parse(text) catch _ because "a failure counts as zero" => 0
  n + fallback()
}
```

```text
The failures of a function parameter belong to your caller, unless its type

  5 │ fn safe(text: str, fallback: fn() -> i64 / raise<ParseError>) -> i64 {
    │                                         ++++++++++++++++++++
```
